title: The Field Brief
blurb: Daily scout surface for CR-Harness and adjacent agent-control research. Public sources only. Not an hourly Cao-style feed — refresh ~daily. Lives under CR-Harness (not hub homepage).

entries.title: LOLPlay: in native League of Legends, higher reasoning effort buys no task success and costs interaction rounds
entries.summary: arXiv:2611.03685. A benchmark in native League of Legends with 36 champion-specific tasks (resource management, combat, cooperation, objectives). Agents act through screenshots and mouse/keyboard; automated initialization and 82 executable subgoal checks separate partial progress from completion. Across 324 task evaluations of three models at three reasoning-effort settings, GPT-6 Astra has the best task success (25.0% at low and medium effort) and best subgoal success (40.3% at medium). High effort improved neither metric over low effort for any model; for Astra, longer requests left fewer interaction rounds. Trajectories show incomplete subgoal composition and actions executing after the observed scene had changed.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Another real-time result saying more thinking per call loses rounds; executable subgoal checks are a cheap way for CR evals to score partial progress instead of only win/loss.

entries.title: KPHarness: probe failures to gather evidence, then accept bounded harness revisions only when paired evals improve
entries.summary: arXiv:2610.27417. Adapts the external execution harness of a frozen vision-language-action model on Minecraft (mining, combat, crafting). Recovery knowledge proposes intervention hypotheses that guide active probing; probe outcomes refine both the knowledge and later probe choice. A slow research loop turns this into bounded harness revisions, each compared with the incumbent under matched sandbox conditions and accepted only when the paired evaluation improves. Reports better task coverage than bare policy execution, a hand-written fixed harness, and knowledge-only evolution, and better completion on unseen tasks with the evolved harness frozen. Numbers not quoted here; abstract only.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Matches how CR-Harness should change itself: revise the harness, not the model, and gate each revision on a paired replay eval against the incumbent.

entries.title: RTSGameAgent: condition-triggered group command plans keep a real-time game running between sparse model calls
entries.summary: arXiv:2606.18950 (v4 dated 3 Nov 2026). RTSGameBench evaluates VLM agents in the open-source RTS Beyond All Reason with full games across 1v1, 2v2, 3v4 and free-for-all match-ups, five diagnostic mini-games and a self-evolving game generator. Its harness, RTSGameAgent, groups units and has the model emit per-group command trajectories as DAGs whose transitions fire on the group's own execution state without another model call, plus replanning triggers for critical events and short/long-term memory. Lv.2 duel ablation: win rate 0.43 full, 0.13 without trajectory planning, 0.07 without group-level control, 0.33 without replanning, 0.20 without memory. The game pauses during inference.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Clash Royale does not pause, so a small plan with explicit fire-conditions executed by the harness between decision_point calls is a direct fit; the ablation says conditional follow-ups and triggers carry most of the gain.

entries.title: StepGate: a calibrated per-step gate hands only uncertain actions from a small local model to a stronger one
entries.summary: arXiv:2610.07816 (Oct 2026). Scores each local SLM action from token uncertainty, tool margin, schema validity, sample consistency, trajectory state and a risk tier, then executes locally, retries once, or escalates that step with a minimized context. On 100 scripted multi-turn tasks (Qwen2.5-1.5B local, 7B strong) it reaches 69.0% trajectory success at 30% cloud actions vs 48.0% local-only, 57.0% query-level routing, 60.0% random escalation and 82.0% strong-only. Authors note the small single-family evaluation and that the gain over random escalation is not significant.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: This is the Jev router at decision_point granularity: keep the fast model on routine placements and escalate only uncertain or high-stakes steps, with a gate fit offline from ETL replays using signals the harness already logs.

entries.title: RLiD: RL directly on the probabilities of a labeled action menu, one forward pass, no invalid actions
entries.summary: arXiv:2611.02455 (submitted 2 Nov 2026). Token-level RL credits the whole generated response, including reasoning and malformed text, although the environment only executes the parsed action. RLiD compiles the observation, an optional compact memory and a labeled action menu into the input and has a large decision model pick an option in a single forward pass, so there is no action parsing and no invalid output. Trained policies are distilled back into generative LLMs. Reported: on ALFWorld the training+distillation pipeline reaches 99.3% success in 12.7 H100 GPU-hours vs 86.6% in 17.3 GPU-hours for token-level RL of the same LLM; with compiled memory a Qwen2.5-1.5B decision model and its distilled LLM reach 100% on all 134 unseen and 140 seen games. Also evaluated on ARC, Countdown and Sokoban.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: This is the CR decision_point shape trained end to end: legal_actions rendered as a labeled menu, the policy scores options instead of writing text. It gives a training path for the Jev router cards and a clean reason to log menu-index actions (not free text) in the ETL.

entries.title: IJev: exactly order-invariant choices by iterated cyclic reordering of the option list
entries.summary: arXiv:2611.01015 (submitted 31 Oct 2026). System-1 decision models answer a choice in one forward pass, but the answer depends on option order and carries a prior over answer labels. Averaging over the K cyclic shifts of one fixed order removes input order but still depends on which cyclic class was chosen. IJev repeatedly reorders options by the cyclic-averaged, label-prior-corrected distribution and re-averages; every iterate is exactly input-order-invariant, and non-converging runs average the rounds. Reported: flip rate zero in every cell over five benchmarks and five models; the default T=20 uniform average improves calibration over a single cyclic average at comparable accuracy. A companion audit (arXiv:2611.00496) finds option swaps flip 0.0-72.6% of choices across typed and prompted setups.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR legal_actions lists have an arbitrary order (hand slot, tile index). Any Jev-style selector over that list should report a flip rate under option permutation; cyclic averaging is a cheap fix to test before trusting probabilities for calibration or abstention.

entries.title: Exo: agents revise their own harness during work, behind a protected mechanism layer; cheaper on an open-world game
entries.summary: arXiv:2611.00463 (submitted 30 Oct 2026; Krentsel, Ratnasamy, Stoica, Casado, Goyal). Exo is an agent runtime that folds harness optimization into task execution: the agent edits its harness and strategies as inspectable code changes, while a minimal protected layer keeps execution history and governs which policy version is active. Reported: on long-running objectives in an open-world game, 12-53% lower model cost than Codex and Pi standalone and 45-82% lower in transfer runs at matched completion; vs the same starting policy without editing, 35-61% lower held-out cost on AppWorld and SREGym with comparable correctness.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: An open-world game result for online harness editing. For CR the useful part is the split: a frozen mechanism layer (action validation, logging, policy activation) that the agent cannot edit, and an editable strategy layer. That boundary is worth fixing before any AutoHarness-style self-editing.

entries.title: ARCBench: after context compaction agents break rules that are still in the summary
entries.summary: arXiv:2611.03223 (submitted 2 Nov 2026). A rule-compliance benchmark on the open-source pi agent harness that measures violations from actions in a tool-calling loop. Finding: compaction rarely deletes the rule; most post-compaction violations happen while the rule is still in the compacted history, with the agent treating a later request as permission. Rule delivery decides whether the agent would break it even without compaction; compaction strategy and budget decide whether the rule survives. The strongest compactor-targeted attack more than doubles violations; runs that keep the rule still violate more than twice as often as full-history runs.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Long CR sessions and long-running coding agents both compact. Keeping a rule in the summary is not enough; hard constraints (legal-move checks, no-force-push, no secrets) belong in the harness, not only in context.

entries.title: Decision models as runtime policy gates for coding agents: explicit example/counterexample boundaries lift recall and cut false alarms
entries.summary: arXiv:2611.02155 (submitted 1 Nov 2026). 22 hosted decision models and two prompted general models were run as classifiers for a 28-rule policy engine over 2,643 synthetic tool calls labeled blind, with a sealed holdout. Explicit boundaries written as examples and counterexamples raised recall by 5.5-26.1 points on all 23 available models and reduced false positives on 21. Jev 1.14: recall 89.3% to 98.2%, unnecessary interruptions 30.6% to 4.8% of 252 clean actions, median latency 120 ms at $0.46 per thousand requests. Dataset, rules and harness are public.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: A measured recipe for the gate pattern already on the board (Jev router, action-class calibration): write rule boundaries as paired examples/counterexamples and report recall plus false-interrupt rate. Applies to the fleet's own agent guardrails as much as to CR.

entries.title: CivHarness / CivTelescope: branch-and-replay from saved Freeciv states trains a pairwise position judge that beats the scoreboard
entries.summary: arXiv:2610.41264 (submitted 30 Oct 2026). Across eight strategy games, the higher-scoring position leads to the worse outcome in 8-68% of position pairs ('scoreboard traps'). CivHarness saves Freeciv states, branches on decisions and replays to future turns for measured long-horizon feedback. CivTelescope, an LLM judge trained on that data, is 1.3-2.0x more accurate than off-the-shelf LLMs on trap pairs and generalizes to new starts, later turns and unseen rules. Used as a dense reward (CivMarshmallow) in mid-game it gives an 8.94-point training gain, 77% above the end-of-game reward; a hybrid schedule scores best over 120 turns.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: The concrete harness the ForeCritic card pointed at: save state, branch, replay, label pairs by real outcome. For CR, elixir/tower-HP scoreboards can trap the same way; a branch-and-replay harness on saved match states could train a pairwise judge for the Jev/plan selector.

entries.title: Gym-Anything-RT: frontier VLM agents pass 9% of real-time minigames vs 75% when the world is paused
entries.summary: arXiv:2610.37567 (submitted 27 Oct 2026). An agentic pipeline generates 100 visual minigames from a six-capability taxonomy for real-time interaction; each can run live, paused, or slowed for controlled comparison. The strongest evaluated agent passes 9.0% in real time vs 75.0% paused. Given code-writing ability, frontier agents write code that bypasses real-time perception and action. Environments are publicly released.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR is real-time: the paused-vs-live gap is the cost the reflex/Jev split is meant to remove. The pause/slow-down knob is a clean ablation design for a CR harness (same states, live vs paused) to measure how much a fast path recovers.

entries.title: Balatro RL: tactical and strategic policies in disjoint phases, with legal-move masking and cross-agent credit
entries.summary: arXiv:2610.39049 (submitted 28 Oct 2026). A Rust simulator state-diffed against the live client, a condensed interface with per-step legal-move masking, and multi-agent PPO split into a tactical blind policy and a strategic shop policy that share state but act in disjoint phases, with per-agent reward routing and explicit cross-agent credit. First-blind clear rate converges above 99%, plateauing at mean max ante 3 of 8; single-agent baselines oscillated between greedy and hoarding and did not stably clear the first blind. The remaining gap is attributed to long-horizon strategy.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Card-game analogue of the strategist/executor split: separate tactical vs strategic policies with routed credit beat one monolithic policy. Supports keeping CR deck/plan choice and in-match placement as distinct decision layers, and a client-diffed simulator as harness infrastructure.

entries.title: World Reward Models (ForeCritic): a 9B typed decision model picks the better candidate directly from executed pairs
entries.summary: arXiv:2610.38439 (submitted 28 Oct 2026). For search-based ML agents, a World Reward Model learns from real execution results to choose which of two candidate programs will perform better, without predicting intermediate outcomes. The authors prove a selector that predicts execution cannot beat the best direct selector on the same inputs. ForeCritic adapts a 9B typed decision model on 5k executed pairs; on 12,438 held-out pairs from 26 ML tasks it picks the better program 79.4% of the time vs 53–62% for general LLM judges, with calibrated probabilities. Inside AIDE, ML-Master and ForeAgent it cuts mean task time 4.4–7.5× while keeping mean scores within 0.01 or raising them.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Same lesson as the Jev router at a different layer: train the pairwise decision from executed outcomes rather than asking an LLM to simulate. For CR, branch-and-execute data (cf. SURE-Act, 10-24) can train a direct move or plan selector.

entries.title: XiangqiBench: finding the move is not winning the game
entries.summary: Chai, Peng, Xiong et al., arXiv:2610.02425 (submitted 1 Oct 2026). Executable Chinese-chess benchmark: from 119 tactical endgames with forced mates, an LLM agent must actually deliver checkmate against an engine defender, through a REPL that separates real moves, state queries and forward simulation. 8,568 multi-turn trajectories from 12 frontier LLMs under two observation protocols. Three gaps: Conversion (models play the stored reference first move in 26.1% of Sighted trials, but only 13.9% of those end in a win); Consistency (leading model 38.7% pass@3 but 5.9% pass^3); Simulation (32.3% of accepted simulation calls stop on an illegal move, and in 49.3% of comparable cases the real defender replies differently from the agent's simulated line).
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Direct warning against scoring CR on per-decision 'good move' metrics alone: decision_point accuracy can look fine while closed-loop match outcomes do not follow. Adopt pass^k (win all k seeds) next to pass@k, separate real actions from state queries/simulation in the action interface, and log illegal actions inside any agent-side lookahead.

entries.title: Kaggle Game Arena tech report: retry/forfeit harness rules as eval design
entries.summary: Doerschuk-Tiberi et al. (Kaggle + Google DeepMind), arXiv:2609.31473 (submitted 25 Sep 2026). Chess, Poker and Werewolf environments with open harness (google-deepmind/game_arena). Chess: legality enforced by the environment; an invalid move gets a bare 'invalid, retry' with diagnostics intentionally hidden, 3 retries, 4th failure = loss; retries ('rethinks') tracked as a reliability metric, and the report finds illegal moves concentrate later in games for weaker models. Poker: one retry, then defaults to check/fold; 20,000 hands per pair, 900,000 hands total, BB/100 with block bootstrap. Werewolf: parse failures past a retry cap force a turn forfeit. Per-game metrics: Bradley–Terry Elo, BB/100, game-theoretic eval.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: The most public, large-scale statement of the design choices CR must make at every decision_point: show the legal list or not, how much feedback on an illegal action, how many retries, and what the fallback is (loss vs conservative default vs forfeit). CR should declare these as a versioned harness policy and log rethink counts by match phase.

entries.title: REFLEX: Jev typed-choice gate + strong-LLM fallback, measured
entries.summary: Wu & Lim (NTU), arXiv:2609.26532 (submitted 22 Sep 2026). REFLEX uses Jev (jev-1.13.0) as a typed decision layer returning (choice, confidence); execute when c≥τ and executable, else fall back to a strong LLM. Frozen 100-task REFLEX-Sim: 95% success vs 88% strong-only with 72.7% fewer strong-model calls at τ=0.5; 66–72% call reduction across Qwen3.8-Max / Kimi K3 / DeepSeek-V4-Pro fallbacks. Honest limits: on BFCL, choosing which function is 98.4% accurate but deciding whether to call any is 52.0%; on τ²-bench a cheap Flash self-escalation cascade stays competitive. Larger action sets (K 10→50) and near-valid competitors reduce accuracy.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: First public controlled evaluation of exactly the jev-gameplay-decision-router idea: typed choice over an allowed set + confidence floor + fallback. Gives CR a metric template (GMR, risk–coverage/AURC, strong calls per success, commit-vs-defer error split) and a warning that legal_actions size and near-valid alternatives degrade the gate.

entries.title: Action-class diagnostic: Acc ≤ GAR exposes act/ask/refuse miscalibration
entries.summary: Zhao et al., arXiv:2609.00949 (1 Sep 2026). Decomposes multi-turn tool-calling failures into action-class miscalibration vs execution failure over TOOL_CALL/ASK/REFUSE/CONFIRM, with an upper bound Acc ≤ Gold Action Recall. Bound violations reveal state graders that mask wrong action classes; context-only perturbations can move accuracy +11.5 vs −21.0 pp across families on the same scenario.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR decision_points also have action classes (play card / wait-noop / escalate). Logging a gold/expected class separately from the chosen action id lets ETL catch outcome graders that reward lucky wins from the wrong class of decision.

entries.title: Jev at decision_point: typed Choice/Noul gate over legal_actions
entries.summary: TypeSafe Jev (OpenRouter typesafe/jev-1.13) returns Choice/Noul/Score with probabilities — no prose. Already LIVE on the fleet harness at confidence_floor 0.55 for CoS routing. Scout ask: wire the same router into Mini Royale gameplay at decision_point (legal_actions whitelist + cockpit path), not hub routing only. Prior art: AutoHarness/PTCG legal masks, R2V residual-risk escalate, confidence-gate act/ask/abstain, HarnessBridge reject-with-feedback.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR already emits decision_point + legal_actions; Jev can Choice among legal ids or Noul-gate escalate/noop when conf<floor, with ETL logging of conf/fallback — reusable eval surface for latency vs false-escalate.

entries.title: AutoHarness: synthesize code that blocks illegal moves
entries.summary: DeepMind (Lou et al.): Gemini-2.5-Flash iteratively synthesizes an is_legal_action / propose_action code harness via Thompson-sampling tree search over environment feedback. Claims 100% legal-action rate across 145 TextArena games; smaller Flash+harness beats larger Pro on many 1P/2P evals. Direct analogue to CR-Harness legal_actions at decision_point.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: CR already whitelists legal_actions — AutoHarness shows how to auto-build or regression-test that verifier from env feedback, and how illegal-move rate dominates LLM game losses.

entries.title: PTCG-Bench: legal-action masking swings card-game ratings
entries.summary: Hua et al.: Pokémon TCG benchmark for LLM agents with modular harness ablations (structured obs, legal-action masking, history). Removing legal-action masking drops Glicko-2 by ~118 points and raises invalid-action rate to ~16%. Self-evolution across rounds stays unstable. Closest public TCG analogue to Mini Royale decision_points.
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Quantifies how much of ‘LLM skill’ is really the mask + observation schema — exactly what CR’s legal_actions + ETL should report per model–harness pair.

entries.title: Adversarial Review: structured disagreement beats naive dual LGTM
entries.summary: Qiu & Gill (arXiv:2608.18167): reviewer + critic protocol; naive AR collapses into false consensus; three-way critic verdicts (AGREE / DISAGREE_EVIDENCE / DISAGREE_CONCERN) lift SWE-PRBench F1. Portable as SKILL.md. Maps onto fleet blind dual-LGTM (Astra + second seat).
entries.why_it_matters_for_cr: Fleet coding loop already wants blind dual LGTM; AR’s typed disagreement is a concrete protocol upgrade for Github Bot EM / Manage review babysitting — also useful when reviewing CR cockpit/eval PRs.
